answers.q1: Maven via the wrapper (primary, and what CI uses). Gradle is a secondary option. Maven has no separate install step, because dependencies resolve on first build. To fetch them up front, run: ./mvnw -B dependency:go-offline. The Gradle equivalent is ./gradlew build.
answers.q2: ./mvnw test (tests only). CI runs the full build with ./mvnw -B verify. Some tests need Docker: MySqlIntegrationTests uses Testcontainers and PostgresIntegrationTests uses Docker Compose.
answers.q4: CI has no separate lint step. Formatting is enforced in Maven's validate phase, through spring-javaformat:validate and the nohttp Checkstyle check, so ./mvnw -B verify (the CI command) runs it. To run only the checks, use ./mvnw -B validate. To fix formatting errors, run ./mvnw spring-javaformat:apply.
answers.q5: Don't hand-edit these generated or vendored paths: target/ and build/ (build output), src/main/resources/static/resources/css (compiled from SCSS by ./mvnw package -P css, so edit the SCSS source instead), and the wrapper files .mvn/wrapper/, mvnw, mvnw.cmd, gradle/wrapper/, gradlew and gradlew.bat. I did not check whether target/, build/ or the css directory exist in this checkout.
